name: Torsemide + Spironolactone
meta: Schedule H – prescription only; Spironolactone: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.
Light cream to light tan crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.

Torsemide (Torasemide): The TRANSFORM-HF trial (2023) found no mortality difference versus furosemide in heart failure, but torsemide offers more predictable absorption and longer action. First approval/introduction: Patented 1974; introduced 1993 (Boehringer Mannheim). Spironolactone: The RALES trial (1999) showed a 30% reduction in mortality in severe HFrEF when spironolactone was added to standard therapy. First approval/introduction: Discovered 1957; introduced 1959 (G. D. Searle & Company).
The loop diuretic produces strong natriuresis; spironolactone blocks aldosterone, conserves potassium (preventing hypokalaemia) and offers prognostic benefit in heart failure and cirrhosis.

Torsemide (Torasemide) Inhibits the Na+/K+/2Cl- co-transporter in the thick ascending loop of Henle, causing natriuresis and diuresis; also mild anti-aldosterone effect and reduction of myocardial fibrosis. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits the Na+/K+/2Cl− co-transporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle; also has anti-aldosterone and anti-fibrotic effects.

Spironolactone Competitively blocks mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptors in the distal tubule and collecting duct, increasing sodium/water excretion and conserving potassium; reduces cardiac fibrosis in heart failure. Receptor / target profile: Competitive mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; moderate androgen receptor antagonist and weak steroidogenesis inhibitor.
Summary: Bioavailability ~80–90% (more predictable than furosemide); Tmax ~1 h. >99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C9. Half-life ~3.5 h (diuretic effect 6–8 h).
Hepatic – deacetylation, S-methylation, hydroxylation (CYP3A4) to active canrenone and 7-alpha-thiomethylspironolactone
Summary: Bioavailability ~90% with food. Rapidly metabolised to active canrenone and 7-alpha-thiomethylspironolactone. Half-life of active metabolites 14–16 h.

Torsemide (Torasemide): With or without food; take in the morning.
Spironolactone: With food (increases absorption); avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes.
Torsemide (Torasemide): Electrolytes (Na, K, Mg), creatinine, uric acid, glucose; weight and fluid status.
Spironolactone: Potassium and creatinine at 3 days, 1 week, then monthly for 3 months, then 3-monthly.

Torsemide (Torasemide): Dehydration, hypovolaemia, hypotension, electrolyte imbalance. Replace fluids and electrolytes. Spironolactone: Drowsiness, confusion, nausea, hyperkalaemia, hyponatraemia. Stop drug; correct electrolytes.
RALES (Pitt et al., NEJM 1999) – spironolactone reduced mortality by 30% in severe heart failure.
Combination diuretic therapy is standard for cirrhotic ascites (EASL/AASLD guidance).

Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
